en.title: Stress in Mă Duc
en.summary: Learn how to connect the weak word mă and the strong word duc smoothly as one spoken unit.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: Listen to the phrase (mă duc) /mə duk/, which means I am going. You say two little words together. The first word is weak and quick. The second word is strong and clear. Together, they sound like one single word. Your voice pushes on the second part.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Start with the small word (mă) /mə/. Relax your mouth and keep your voice light. Make the sound very short. Now move quickly to the word (duc) /duk/. Round your lips for this part. Put all your energy here. Raise your pitch slightly on this final beat.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: When you see (mă duc) /mə duk/, do not stop between words. Read them as one smooth rhythm unit. The letter ă is a soft, resting sound. It never takes the stress in this phrase. The main beat always lands on the letter u.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not stress both words equally. If you emphasize the first word, you break the flow. Do not pause between the two parts. Do not make the first sound too loud or long. Keep the first beat weak and jump straight to the strong finish.
